newsitem.title: UK: London gold turns easier at afternoon fixing.
newsitem.headline: London gold turns easier at afternoon fixing.

text.p: Precious metals prices edged lower on Tuesday afternoon as gold ran into resistance and a consistently strong dollar put on the pressure, dealers said.
Gold had been half-hearted in its challenge of $363.00-$364.00 resistance earlier and the buyers had little answer when New York dipped lower than expected in its opening exchanges.
"It's been quiet yesterday and today but the volatility will continue although it may take a couple of days," one dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $359.40 per ounce following $361.75 in the morning and $362.15 on Monday afternoon. The Comex April contract was down $2.80 at $361.00 at the 1500 GMT fixing.

The dollar was off its 34-month peak versus the mark but still firm. Foreign exchange dealers said the market was being sustained by dealings involving U.S/German yield spreads ahead of jobs data from these countries later this week.

Since bullion bottomed at its 3-3/4 year low on February 12 at $336.90 it has climbed to within $5.00 of its opening year level (the Jan 2 fix was $367.80, the 1997 high) driven by fund short covering, dealers said.
Meanwhile Comex's "large trader" net short positions fell to 21,241 contracts by February 25 from 46,650 two weeks earlier, data by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission showed
"Fund short covering will dominate the market. The producers may see the rise and sell into so we could have a volatile price," one dealer said.
Nevertheless the fund-driven momentum could take gold prices through the $370s, the dealer said. Meanwhile gold was seen in a range of $358.00-$364.00 helped by physical support.
Silver was marked down with gold to $5.25/$5.27 having seen most of its action late on Monday in New York when it was bought up to about $5.40 and promptly sold into.
On Monday the gold-silver ratio was about 68 having gone from 65 to 70 mid February before being sold off.
"If it goes below 64, it could be heading for 57.30," said technical analyst Karen Jones at Credit Suisse First Boston.
Palladium was steady at $151.25/$152.25, $3.25 down on Monday's close. "Palladium is probably supporting the whole complex," one dealer said.
Mixed reports on the severity and impact of a strike at Russia's Norislk plant this month and the still delayed start to Russia-Japan supply talks underpin the price, dealers said.
